intro: Abbreviations and acronyms, capital letters, and the punctuation marks that work differently in Spanish.
p.abreviatura.consejo: It ends in a full stop: «Sr.», «pág.». The full word is read: «Sr.» is read «señor».
p.sigla.consejo: It has no full stops and does not change in the plural: «la RAE», «los AVE». The gender is that of the main word.
p.mayúscula.consejo: It is used at the start of a sentence and in proper names. It keeps its tilde: «África», «Ángel».
p.minúscula.consejo: In Spanish days, months and languages take lowercase: «lunes», «enero», «español».
p.comillas.consejo: Always plural. Spanish prefers the angle ones: «like this». The full stop goes after closing them.
p.raya.consejo: In a novel, the «raya» introduces each speech. It is not the same as the hyphen (-), which is shorter.
p.signo.consejo: The question and exclamation marks come in pairs: they open «¿ ¡» and close «? !».
p.saludo.consejo: In a formal letter, a colon follows the greeting: «Estimado señor López:».
p.apellido.consejo: In Spain almost everyone has two surnames: the father's and the mother's. The ll sounds like y.
p.dos puntos.consejo: They follow the greeting of a letter and come before a list or a quotation.
p.punto y coma.consejo: It separates long parts of a sentence. It marks a pause stronger than a comma and softer than a full stop.
p.puntos suspensivos.consejo: There are always three. They leave a sentence unfinished or show doubt: «No sé…».
b1.texto:
**Abbreviations** shorten a word and end in a full stop: **Sr.**, **Sra.**, **Dr.**, **Ud.**, **pág.**, **tel.**, **avda.** (avenida), **c/** (calle), **p. ej.**, **etc.** They are read as the full word: **Sr.** is read **señor**. The plural adds **-s** (**págs.**, **Sres.**, **Uds.**) or doubles the letter when there is only one: **EE. UU.**, **JJ. OO.**, **RR. HH.**

**Acronyms** are made of initials, without full stops: **RAE**, **AVE**, **DNI**, **ESO**, **ADN**, **ITV**, **DGT**. They take the gender of the main word: **la** ESO (la educación), **el** DNI (el documento), **la** RAE (la academia). They do not change in the plural: **los AVE**, never «AVEs». Some are read as a word (**el AVE**, **la RAE**) and others letter by letter (**el DNI**: de-ene-i).

**Capital letters: fewer than in English.** These take a **small letter**: days and months (**lunes**, **enero**), languages and nationalities (**español**, **una chica francesa**), titles before a name (**el señor García**, **el doctor Ruiz**) and the words of a title after the first (**Cien años de soledad**). These take a **capital**: names of people and places, institutions (**el Museo del Prado**) and festivals (**Navidad**). Capitals keep their tilde: **Ángel**, **África**.

**Punctuation.** **¿ ?** and **¡ !** open and close. Spanish prefers angle **quotation marks** **«like this»**. The **dash** (**—**) introduces each speech in a novel. A colon follows the greeting of a letter: **Querida Ana:** Numbers take a point for thousands and a comma for decimals: **1.500,75**. **Ellipsis** is always three dots. And there is no comma before **y** in a list: pan, queso y vino.
b2.f0.texto: I am writing a formal letter to Mr. López.
b2.f1.texto: Put the abbreviation «Sr.» before the surname.
b2.f2.texto: That abbreviation is pronounced like the full word.
b2.f3.texto: Do the days of the week take a capital letter?
b2.f4.texto: They take a small letter, just like languages and months.
b2.f5.texto: Which mark goes after the greeting?
b2.f6.texto: After the greeting go two dots (a colon).
b2.f7.texto: Tomorrow I take the letter to Seville on the AVE.
b4.texto:
**Acronyms: gender and plural.** An acronym takes the gender of its main word and does not change in the plural.

- **La** RAE (la Real Academia Española)
- **El** AVE (el tren de Alta Velocidad Española) → **los** AVE
- **El** DNI (el documento nacional de identidad) → **los** DNI
- **La** ESO (la Educación Secundaria Obligatoria)

**Abbreviations: full stop and plural.** They always take a full stop. The plural doubles the letter or adds -s: **EE. UU.**, **págs.**, **Sres.**

**Capital or small letter.** Ask yourself what the word is: if it is a proper name (**Madrid**, **López**, **Navidad**), a capital. If it is a day, a month, a language or a nationality, a small letter: **el lunes**, **una profesora francesa**.

**After the greeting**, a colon, and a capital or a small letter depending on the style: **Estimado señor López:**
b4.e0.texto: The RAE explains the rules of Spanish.
b4.e1.texto: The AVE trains leave the station on time.
b4.e2.texto: Mr. López writes his name with a capital letter.
b5.f0.texto: The AVE arrives at the station amid a murmur of wheels.
b5.f1.texto: The travellers step down slowly with their suitcases and their newspapers.
b5.f2.texto: A big clock shows eight in the morning over the platform.
b5.f3.texto: On a blue sign shine big white letters.
b5.f4.texto: A calm voice announces the departures of the day.
b5.f5.texto: Elena walks among the crowd with a letter in her hand.
b5.f6.texto: On the envelope gleams the black ink of each capital letter.
b5.f7.texto: An elderly man in a hat greets her from the bench.
b5.f8.texto: She smiles and puts the letter in her bag.
b5.f9.texto: Behind her, the train waits with its doors open.
b6.o0.refuerzo: An abbreviation is read as the full word.
b6.o2.refuerzo: No: in Spanish it is read «señor».
b7.o0.refuerzo: An acronym takes the gender of its main word, and «educación» is feminine.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done: the main word, «educación», is feminine.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is singular: it is one stage of education.
b7.pregunta: ESO comes from «educación». Which article is missing?
b8.o0.refuerzo: Spanish does not add -s to acronyms.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Neither is -es added: the acronym does not change.
b8.o2.refuerzo: That is it: acronyms do not change in the plural.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: in Spanish, a colon follows the greeting.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The comma is the English custom. Spanish uses a colon.
b9.o2.refuerzo: A full stop would close the sentence, and the greeting is only the start.
b9.pregunta: Complete the greeting with the right mark.
b10.o0: El Lunes hablo con una profesora Francesa.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Neither days nor nationalities take a capital.
b10.o1: El lunes hablo con una profesora francesa.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is it: day and nationality, with a small letter.
b10.o2: el lunes hablo con una profesora francesa.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Every sentence begins with a capital.
b10.pregunta: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
b11.frase: El lunes hablo con una profesora francesa
b11.traduccion: On Monday I talk to a French teacher
b12.o0.refuerzo: That is it: a point for thousands and a comma for decimals.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is the English system, the other way round.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The apostrophe is not used for decimals.
b12.pregunta: How does Spanish write one thousand five hundred point seven five?
b13.pregunta: Write the acronym of «Real Academia Española».
p.formal.consejo: In Spanish «formal» is written and said the same way as in English, with the stress at the end.
p.reglas.consejo: Plural of «regla». The initial «r» is strong: «RRE-glas», with the stress on the first syllable.
p.salen.consejo: From «salir», to go out. The plural ending «-en» is used with «ellos» or «ustedes».
p.puntuales.consejo: From «punto», a point or a precise moment. The stress falls on «TWA», the «ua» forms a diphthong.
p.anuncia.consejo: From «anuncio», an announcement. The «ia» at the end is a diphthong, read as «thya».
p.salidas.consejo: Plural of «salida», exit or departure. The word comes from «salir», to go out.
p.señor.consejo: The «ñ» sounds like the «ny» in «canyon». The short form is «Sr.»
p.cursos.consejo: Plural of «curso». Spanish schools count their levels by «cursos», each one a school year.
p.periódicos.consejo: Plural of «periódico». The «io» in «periódico» forms a diphthong, pronounced «rjo».
